articleTitle: Revitalizing Historical Paintings through Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper explores the innovative application of artificial intelligence (AI) in the revitalization of historical paintings, addressing the challenges of traditional restoration and enhancing preservation techniques. By leveraging advanced AI models, such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), style transfer, and inpainting algorithms, this research demonstrates how machine learning can reconstruct, enhance, and restore artworks with remarkable detail and accuracy. Utilizing datasets of historical paintings, AI systems are trained to reproduce textures, restore faded colors, and even repair damaged sections, maintaining the authenticity of original masterpieces. Quantitative analyses, including image quality metrics like PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) and SSIM (Structural Similarity Index), are conducted to compare AI-restored paintings with manually restored versions. Results indicate that AI-driven methods achieve high fidelity in texture and color restoration, offering a cost-effective and scalable solution for cultural preservation. The study concludes with a discussion on the potential applications of AI in museums and digital archives, emphasizing AI’s transformative role in art conservation. Future research could extend these findings by addressing ethical considerations and collaborating closely with art historians to further refine AI’s role in cultural heritage.

articleTitle: Improved Cotton Leaf Disease Classification Using Parameter-Efficient Deep Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Cotton crops, often called “white gold”, face significant production challenges, primarily due to various leaf-affecting diseases. As a major global source of fiber, timely and accurate disease identification is crucial to ensure optimal yields and maintain crop health. While deep learning and machine learning techniques have been explored to address this challenge, there remains a gap in developing lightweight models with fewer parameters which could be computationally effective for agricultural practitioners. To address this, we propose an innovative deep learning framework integrating a subset of trainable layers from MobileNet, transfer learning, data augmentation, a learning rate decay schedule, model checkpoints, and early stopping mechanisms. Our model demonstrates exceptional performance, accurately classifying seven cotton disease types with an overall accuracy of 98.42% and class-wise precision ranging from 96% to 100%. This results in significantly enhanced efficiency, surpassing recent approaches i n accuracy and model complexity. The existing models in the literature have yet to attain such high accuracy, even when tested on data sets with fewer disease types. The substantial performance improvement, combined with the lightweight nature of the model, makes it practically suitable for real-world applications in smart farming. By offering a high-performing and efficient solution, our framework can potentially address challenges in cotton cultivation, contributing to sustainable agricultural practices.

articleTitle: The Role of Digital Transformation and Bank Size in Enhancing Customer Trust and Banking Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Digital transformation (DITR) and bank size (SIZE) are critical determinants of trust (TRUST) and banking performance (PERF). This study investigates the relationship between these variables, emphasizing how TRUST positively impacts PERF by reducing non-performing loans (NPLs) and enhancing operational efficiency. By synthesizing findings from recent literature and analyzing observed banking data, this study highlights the complementary roles of DITR and SIZE in fostering TRUST and improving PERF. The results underscore the strategic importance of digital transformation and organizational scale in enhancing customer confidence and achieving sustainable banking performance.

articleTitle: A Case Study on Customer Knowledge Management Model to Enhance Social Media Marketing Strategies of Chinese Hotpot Restaurant in Chiang Mai
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The Chinese Hotpot Restaurant in Chiangmai lacks efficient marketing strategies to attract Chinese customers. The study aims to bridge the gap between customer expectations and business offerings by utilizing Customer Knowledge Management principles, thereby improving Chinese customer satisfaction. Text analysis and Kano model are used as tools to analyze and prioritize knowledge about customer and knowledge from customer. Then, the research design strategies for knowledge for customer to enhance customer experience. The outcome is to propose social media marketing strategies to help Chinese hotpot restaurant improve its service and market competitiveness. Lessons learned from the case study can be generalized to similar businesses in the catering industry.

articleTitle: LINE Sticker Design to Promote Tourism in Chiang Rai Province "The Four Sacred Legends of Lanna"
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The aims of this research are as follows: 1) To study the stories of the Four Sacred Legendary Beliefs of Lanna to promote tourism in Chiang Rai Province. 2) To develop LINE stickers featuring the Four Sacred Legendary Beliefs of Lanna to promote tourism in Chiang Rai Province. 3) To evaluate the satisfaction of the sample group towards the LINE stickers of the Four Sacred Legendary Beliefs of Lanna for promoting tourism in Chiang Rai Province, including experts in LINE sticker design and character design. The sample group consisted of 100 people who use the LINE application. The research tools were unstructured interview forms and satisfaction questionnaires. The results revealed that the four most interesting legendary sacred objects among the sample group were 1) Si Hu Ha Ta, 2) Chang Ngu, 3) Pla Lai Phueak, and 4) Mom, respectively. These were used as guidelines for designing characters and poses for the LINE stickers. The researcher then designed the characters, resulting in LINE stickers with 4 characters, each having 16 poses. The overall satisfaction evaluation of the LINE stickers featuring the Four Sacred Legendary Beliefs of Lanna for promoting tourism in Chiang Rai Province was at the highest level $({{\bar x}} = 4.67)$.

articleTitle: Development of an E-commerce System for Designing Identity Patterns of Community and Ethnic Group Products
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research aims to collect data on the traditional identity fabric patterns of ethnic groups. Specifically, it gathers 18 fabric patterns from the hmong ethnic group and 16 fabric patterns from the mien ethnic group. The collected data will be stored in a database system designed for e-commerce. Additionally, the study analyzes the factors influencing user satisfaction with an e-commerce in website www.pyhill.com using a sample size of 400 participants. The research found that customers are most satisfied with the ability to design unique ethnic products that are one-of-a-kind. In order of impact, the factors influencing product purchase decisions through the www.pyhill.com system are as follows. 1) The ability to design product patterns themselves, which has the highest impact on user satisfaction. 2) Products designed to be unique and not available in the market. 3) Products that are distinctive and reflect the identity of the ethnic group. 4) The reliability of the product delivery system for pre-ordered items. These factors are statistically significant at 0.05 with a 95% confidence level.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition Using EEG Signals in Human Brain Waves and Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Emotion recognition using EEG signals has gained growing attention in recent years due to its promising applications in human-computer interaction, affective computing, and mental health assessment. This study investigates the performance of various deep learning architectures in classifying emotional states from EEG recordings. We utilize the Emotion EEG dataset as a benchmark and evaluate five prominent deep learning models. The classification task targets three emotion categories: neu-tral, positive, and negative. Experimental results reveal notable differences in model performance. Among the tested models, BiGRU achieves the highest classification accuracy of 97.70% (±0.69%), followed closely by BiLSTM with 97.37% (±0.17%). These bidirectional architectures significantly outperform the CNN model, which attains an accuracy of only 61.59% (±1.22%). The LSTM and GRU models yield intermediate results, nearing 92% accuracy. The findings highlight the effectiveness of bidirectional recurrent neural networks in modeling the temporal characteristics of EEG signals for emotion detection. This research contributes to advancing EEG-based emotion recognition by identifying the most suitable deep learning strategies, thus supporting the development of more intelligent and emotion-aware computing systems.

articleTitle: The Comparative Study of Artificial Intelligence Techniques: DeepMotion vs. Autodesk Maya in Enhancing 3D Animation Creation and Learning Experiences
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of traditional software (Autodesk Maya) versus AI-powered tools (DeepMotion) in the creation of 3D animations, focusing on learner engagement, personalized learning, and performance outcomes. The research employs a quasi-experimental design with a mixed-methods approach, combining action research and surveys. Sixteen purposively selected participants with baseline knowledge in digital arts were assessed using a Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) framework before and after engagement with both tools. The study defines efficiency in terms of time and quality, comparing the ability of Autodesk Maya and DeepMotion to produce high-quality animations efficiently. Results indicate that Autodesk Maya produces higher-quality animations, while DeepMotion significantly reduces time utilization, making it almost ten times more efficient than Maya (efficiency scores of 0.896 vs. 8.609, respectively). Two-sample t-tests reveal statistically significant differences (p < 0.01) in both quality and time efficiency between the two tools. These findings highlight the complementary strengths of each tool—Maya's superior quality versus DeepMotion's time efficiency—suggesting that the choice of software should align with user priorities, whether emphasizing animation detail or production speed.

articleTitle: The Design and Development of Media Formats for Public Relations Books and Applications Using Augmented Reality Technology to Promote Tourism in Chiang Rai Province
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The use of AR technology in designing books and applications, as well as designing representative symbols to promote tourism in Chiang Rai Province, is expected to be highly effective in the coming years. Augmented reality (AR) media selected by the researchers highlight tourist destinations known and distinctive to each area. Symbols representing the 10 districts of Chiang Rai Province were created, such as (1) Mueang Chiang Rai District using the symbol of King Mengrai, (2) Mae Chan District with the Mexican Sunflower, (3) Mae Fa Luang District with the Cherry Blossom, (4) Chiang Saen District with the Naga, (5) Chiang Khong District with the Giant Catfish, (6) Wiang Pa Pao District with the Hot Spring, (7) Thoeng District with Phu Chi Fa, (8) Phaya Mengrai District with the Fighting Cock, (9) Wiang Chai District with Lord Gu Na, and (10) Paan District with the Beautiful Woman. The satisfaction level with the use of books and applications combined with AR technology for promoting tourism in Chiang Rai Province was very high $\left({{{\bar X}} = 4.56}\right)$. The media was highly capable of attracting and satisfying tourists, particularly with the appealing content of tourist locations and the 3D characters for each district. Because it incorporates AR technology, which differentiates it from traditional, conventional media, it becomes more interesting to tourists.

articleTitle: Fashion Knowledge Management for Business Decision Making (Women Apparel on Zalora Indonesia)
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study investigates knowledge management and fashion analysis in women's apparel on Zalora Indonesia, utilizing data collected from April to September 2024. The research employs a descriptive analysis approach. There are five analyses discussed in this article, including subcategory and region analysis, product analysis, characteristics analysis, price analysis, and customer analysis. Details like the top-selling subcategories, product color trends, material breakdowns, size, price and discount, occasions, customer gender, age and payment method are all revealed by the analysis. Based on Zalora sales data, knowledge management (KM) strategies for MSMEs in Indonesian women apparel includes: 1) R&D and production (focus on dress and tops as best GMV categories; plain and natural colors for color offerings; casual, work wear, and special occasions dresses for product offerings; cotton as the main material, M size clothing); 2) Marketing (discount 70% and up always sell; focus on price tier between EUR15-29 during economy slowdown; focus on female customers age 31-40 years for bigger purchasing power; more sales form outskirts customers; 3) Information Technology (bank transfer and credit card are still primary payment methods, but start offering pay-later payment method as it gains more popularity; and sole focus on mobile commerce). This article aims to provide useful knowledge to help stakeholders involved in the fashion industry especially MSMEs (Micro Small and Medium Enterprises) as a guide to create better business strategies.

articleTitle: Knowledge Audit and Gap Analysis for Strategic Classroom Activities: Improving Active Listening in Lower Grade Students
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study focuses on the improvement of active listening ability of lower grade students in primary schools, and analyzes the key strategic knowledge of teachers in classroom activity management to improve students' active listening ability combined with knowledge audit and gap analysis. Through knowledge audit and gap analysis, four major problems of students' listening ability are identified, and three core strategies are selected through Pareto analysis and scope conference: creative teaching methods, goal-oriented management and question design. In addition, 10 experts were selected to participate in the study, which laid a foundation for the subsequent transformation and promotion of strategic knowledge combined with SECI model. This study can not only provide practical guidance for primary education, but also provide useful reference for active listening training in enterprise management, human resources training and other fields, and provide new ideas for improving education quality and cross-field communication efficiency.

articleTitle: Multimedia Learning Theory for Intelligent Teaching Software Evaluation in Chinese Language Courses of Thai Primary Schools
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study explores the application of Multimedia Learning Theory (MLT) in evaluating intelligent Chinese teaching software for second-grade Thai primary school students. The research aims to determine the suitability of three software applications—Wukong, Duolingo, and Super Chinese—based on their media element indices. Through a mixed-methods approach combining qualitative and quantitative research, 30 students were divided into three groups, each using one application over six weeks. Pre- and post-tests assessed listening and speaking skills, while student feedback was gathered through satisfaction surveys. The study's findings are expected to provide empirical evidence on the effectiveness of multimedia elements in enhancing language acquisition, aiding educators in selecting appropriate teaching software aligned with Thai primary school curriculum goals. The results will offer practical insights into improving Chinese language instruction through tailored multimedia integration.

articleTitle: The Research of Chinese Telemedicine Platform Based on the Competitive Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Based on the Competitive Analysis theory, this study explores the user experience of Chinese online medical platform through KANO Model. In recent years, with the outbreak of COVID-19, the limitations of the traditional medical industry, the progress of technology, and the launch of various policies conducive to telemedicine, online medical industry have developed rapidly in China. However, due to the low threshold of entry, many similar platforms appear in the market, resulting in homogenization problems. The aim of this study is to help the platform provide products that are more in line with user expectations and achieve competitive advantages. Therefore, the study identify the factors of user demand through interviews, collect data through questionnaires, and use SPSS analysis software to process and calculate usage data based on the Better-Worse coefficient. According to the calculation of 30 collected demand elements, the coordinate chart is drawn to show the relationship between user satisfaction and provided service. Furthermore, to complete the collection, analysis and classification of user data, and extract the user needs of Chinese online medical platform, so as to provide reference for the functional service setting of telemedicine platform.

articleTitle: Touch Sensors for Safety in Industrial Automation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper designs and evaluates a touch sensor based on a MOSFET that detects electric fields generated between mechanisms in industrial automation systems and human skin. The sensor aims to enhance safety in industrial operations. When the sensor installed on an automated mechanism comes into contact with human skin, it detects the electric field and electrostatic discharge. The processor immediately halts the automation or robotic system to ensure worker safety. The best test results indicate that the sensor operates with a response time of 3 milliseconds.

articleTitle: Smart Web Application for Recommending the Selection of Equipment for Organizing Activities in Educational Institutions
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Higher education institutions strive to improve the quality of instruction and research to prepare students with essential 21st-century competencies. They promote academic and professional growth through teaching, research initiatives, community engagement, and the preservation of cultural values. One key tool in this effort is an educational resource recommendation system, critical in boosting students’ academic outcomes, stimulating engagement in learning activities, and elevating educational standards. This study presents the design and evaluation of a personalized recommendation system for online educational resources, leveraging web technologies and mining techniques integrated within a digital learning infrastructure. The proposed system enhances the intelligence and adaptability of the network-based educational platform, caters to students’ personalized learning requirements, and streamlines the process of accessing relevant information by minimizing the time required for resource discovery.

articleTitle: Automated Framework for Active Directory Security and Compliance through Continuous Monitoring and Attack Path Validation
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: As cyber threats get more sophisticated and the attack surface expands, Active Directory (AD) has become a prominent target for attackers. Compromising AD can result in major security breaches and regulatory issues. This paper provides an automated AD security and compliance system that uses continuous monitoring security compliance and attack path validation to improve enterprises’ security posture. By continuously monitoring AD’s security posture and simulating real-world attack scenarios, the framework detects vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and potential attack pathways in real-time. This proactive approach helps firms to discover and address security problems quickly, maintaining regulatory compliance and protecting vital assets. The framework’s automated features decrease the strain on security teams while also providing a full view of the AD environment, allowing for informed decision-making and effective risk management.

articleTitle: Development of Automatic Cartesian Robot Cannabis Seeder using LabVIEW
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This article describes the invention of autonomous cannabis seeding equipment to reduce contamination and planting time. The automated cannabis seeder employs an NI myRIO control board to operate a y-axis stepper motor attached to a ball screw to move along the breadth of each row of 14 seed trays. Soil drilling and burial Drill all holes at the same depth. This promotes seed germination and lowers human-seed germ contamination. These 7 soil drill heads and 7 seeders use 3D printers to design and shape the workpiece. An 800-watt air pump smokes the cannabis seeds. Linear electric motors function in two rows in the z-axis. The buffer reverses the drowning process from row 14 to the first row, starting from the 3rd row and continuing through the final series of steps until 14 rows in the y-axis are complete. The hardware controls all program activities in LabVIEW. We tested the automated cannabis seeding machine 100 times on average, sowing cannabis seeds into 98 seed trays and dropping 93 seeds at 94.80% efficiency in 10.38 minutes. A 16 percent faster machine than human work is available.

articleTitle: Study of CVS Causes and Prevention using Two-Factor Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Tablets, as thin, portable digital devices, are widely used by students for educational purposes. However, prolonged and continuous use can lead to computer vision syndrome (CVS), a condition characterized by visual and physical discomfort. Ergonomic practices and the use of accessories have been suggested to mitigate the risk of CVS. This study aims to analyze factors that help prevent CVS among tablet users. A cross-sectional, online questionnaire-based study was conducted among university students in Central Thailand. A total of 199 students aged 13–26 years, who owned and used tablets, participated in the study. The average daily tablet usage was ≤6 hours. Among the participants, 69 students reported taking 15-minute breaks during study sessions, while 82 adhered to ergonomic practices, such as maintaining a one-cubit distance from the tablet screen. CVS symptoms were reported by 62% of students, with a significant correlation to inadequate rest breaks. Notably, 73% of female students reported experiencing CVS symptoms. The findings indicate that longer durations of tablet use and insufficient rest breaks significantly increase the risk of CVS among university students. Adopting proper ergonomic habits and regular rest breaks is essential to reduce this risk.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity Awareness Among Users and Employees: A Practical Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research explores how susceptible employees in a particular organization are to phishing attacks. This was done by sending out fake emails designed to look like phishing attempts. Out of over 12,000 emails sent, roughly a quarter of people clicked on the links within them, and 12% even gave away personal information. Interestingly, those working in technical roles like IT were actually more likely to fall for these tricks than people in non-technical roles. Employees as a whole were even more likely to click links and give away information than other users. This study highlights the importance of ongoing, tailored cybersecurity training for everyone in an organization, especially those in technical roles. The study was conducted ethically, ensuring everyone’s privacy. Based on the findings, the researchers provided suggestions for improving cybersecurity and ideas for future research.

articleTitle: Inspiring Creativity: A Comparative Study of Hands-On Artifact Interaction and 3D Art Viewing
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The use of 3D technology in creative processes not only facilitates the creation of complex and intricate works but also provides opportunities for creators to experiment and develop unique and engaging concepts. Additionally, multimedia and 3D technology enhance the diversity and interest of the audience's experience. This study focuses on comparing the impact of using 3D models versus viewing ancient artifacts in traditional formats on enhancing creativity among students in different groups. Descriptive data analysis revealed that both groups had equal mean outputs (7.14 pieces per person), but the group using 3D models (Group 2) showed greater consistency in their work, with lower variance (5.14) and standard deviation (2.27) compared to the group using traditional visuals (Group 1), which had higher variance (27.24) and standard deviation (5.22).The findings suggest that implementing 3D technology in education goes beyond preserving historical information - it serves as a crucial tool for stimulating creativity and fostering innovation. This technology enables the development of immersive learning environments that can adapt to individual learning styles while promoting collaborative and cross-disciplinary approaches to education.

articleTitle: Eliciting Factor Influences in Using AI Cross-cultural Communication Translation of Chinese Student Through Text Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: With the continuous development of artificial intelligence translation technology, AI translation tools have become an important auxiliary tool for cross-cultural communication among Chinese students in Thailand. Through text analysis method, this paper analyzes the key factors for Chinese students in Thailand to choose AI translation software. Through collecting and analyzing 80 comments data from social platforms, this paper adopts keyword extraction Techniques such as word frequency analysis and sentiment analysis reveal the core needs and main problems that international students pay attention to when choosing translation tools. The research finds that translation accuracy and context adaptability are the most important factors for international students to choose translation tools, while translation errors and cultural background differences are the main pain points. The results of this study has a deeper understanding of how Chinese students develop and use AI translation software, and provide optimization suggestions for the developers of AI translation tools.

articleTitle: MHICuS-Based Fourth-Order Active Band-Pass Filter Design Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: In this article, the meta-hybrid intensified current search (MHICuS), one of the most efficient metaheuristic optimization techniques, is applied to optimally design the fourth-order active band-pass filter. The structure of the considered fourth-order band-pass filter aligns the Sallen-Key topology. Results obtained by the MHICuS will be compared with those obtained by the classical technique using the Butterworth filter coefficient comparison principle. As results, it was found that the fourth-order active band-pass filter designed by the MHICuS provides very satisfactory frequency response with closer to the ideal response than the classical technique using the Butterworth filter coefficient comparison principle.

articleTitle: Solving Optimization Problems by a Hybrid Algorithm Based on Sand Cat Swarm Optimization and Invasive Weed Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper addresses an optimization problem using hybrid algorithms of the Sand Cat Swarm Optimization (SCSO) and Invasive Weed Optimization (IWO). In this study, the reproduction step in the IWO algorithm was incorporated after the initial population step of the SCSO. The proposed algorithm was compared against the following: Intersection Mutation Differential Evolution (IMDE), Differential Evolution (DE), SCSO, and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), whereby the performance was tested on six benchmark functions using a 10-fold cross validation. The results indicate that the proposed algorithm yielded the optimal solution for two out of the six benchmark functions. Additionally, when compared with the other four chosen algorithms, it yielded the best overall results. The findings suggest that the proposed algorithm is able to generate solutions similar to those obtained from the previous methods, essentially for the continuous step function, the multimodal function, and the discontinuous step function.

articleTitle: Image-Mixed Glitch Sounds
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Glitch art is the art that uses errors (glitches) in images, videos, and sounds that are intentionally created by destroying digital data or physically manipulating electronic devices. This type of glitch art is interesting in that it expresses unpredictable, accidental beauty. We are exploring the methods and effects of creating glitch art, and as part of this research, we attempted to create glitch sounds by mixing sound and images. Specifically, we simultaneously loaded image and sound data into the image processing software Photoshop to create multi-layered data. This generates glitches in the sound data. Our goal is not to generate glitch sounds using a random method, but rather to generate glitch sounds using a method based on legitimate manipulation of images, which are on a different level from sound, and to make the glitch sound visually enjoyable. We have confirmed that this goal can be achieved using the method used in this research. This research is unique in that it simultaneously realizes the audibility and visualization of glitches, and creates a new type of art that brings about a shift in aesthetic sensibilities.

articleTitle: Prism-Shaped Dielectric Resonator Circularly Polarized Antenna with Loop-Shaped Metasurface-Enhanced Reflector
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a prism-shaped dielectric resonator (DR) -based antenna with circularly polarized (CP) characteristics for C-band wireless systems. This antenna comprised a prism-shaped DR and single-layer substrate. The prism-shaped DR is on the upper-side substrate. Besides, a rod-shaped probe was plugged into a DR and connected by an SMA connector on the lower-side substrate. A loop-shaped metasurface-enhanced reflector is employed to improve bandwidth (i.e., RLBW and ARBW) and antenna gain. A regularly spaced array of 7 × 7 loop-shaped metasurface unit structures is positioned on the upper substrate side. The simulation RLBW and ARBW results at 5.8 GHz (center frequency) are 34% (5.22 – 7.2 GHz) and 16% (5.27 – 6.2 GHz). This antenna radiates left-hand circular polarization with an optimal maximum gain at 5.5 GHz of 6.7 dBic, making it suitable for C-band wireless networks.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Sequentially-Rotated Cubic-Shaped Dielectric Resonator Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study proposes a cubic-shaped dielectric resonator (DR) broadband circularly polarized (CP) array antenna for S-band networks. The design includes 2 × 2 cubic-shaped DR units and a substrate. The upper and lower substrates feature a split-annular aperture ground plane and a sequential-phase feed. Employing the sequential-phase feed, the proposed array antenna aims to enhance performance metrics, including RLBW, ARBW, and antenna gain. Simulation results indicate a RLBW of 56.25% (2.25 – 3.6 GHz) and an ARBW of 43.33% (2.38 – 3.42 GHz). The optimal gain achieved is 9.14 dBic at 3.3 GHz. Furthermore, the array antenna demonstrates right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) characteristics, rendering it suitable for S-band technology.

articleTitle: Optimizing Cocoa Pod Harvest Timing Using the SIMPLE Model: Calibration and Performance Evaluation Across Colombian Regions
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of the SIMPLE model for predicting cocoa pod harvest timing across five regions in Colombia. Utilizing daily weather data from January 1, 2018, to December 31, 2020, and transforming it into .In WHT files, the model incorporates key input variables, including flowering date, solar radiation ( SRAD), maximum and minimum temperatures (TMAX, TMIN), and rainfall. The research focused on three regional parameters—thermal time required for pod harvest (Tsum), Radiation Use Efficiency (RUE), and yield—while common physiological parameters were used across regions. Calibration was performed for cultivars ICS95 and CCN51, with a crop cycle set to 200 days from flowering to harvest, though farmers traditionally harvest at 180 days. Model performance was assessed using the relative root mean square error (RRMSE) by comparing simulated yields with field data from Fedecacao. Results indicate that the SIMPLE model effectively predicts cocoa yield with an overall RRMSE of 7.2%, outperforming other crop models. The model demonstrated variations in thermal time and yield across regions, highlighting that harvest timing can be optimized based on regional temperature and solar radiation patterns. The study also identified the potential for improved cocoa quality and yield predictions by considering environmental effects on fruit development. Future work will focus on incorporating additional factors such as diseases and nutritional deficiencies and developing an accessible app for farmers to enhance decision-making.

articleTitle: Mype Navigator System for Teaching Financial Education to Micro and Small Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study introduces the Mype Navigator System, a Learning Management System (LMS) designed to provide financial education to Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) in Lima, Peru. The effectiveness of the Mype Navigator System was evaluated by comparing the performance of two groups of MSEs using this system against those taught through traditional methods. The results indicate that users of the Mype Navigator System improved their average scores from 15.5 to 17.5 points, representing a 10% increase, which confirms the system's effectiveness. Additionally, a usability assessment was conducted using the System Usability Scale (SUS), and the Mype Navigator System achieved an impressive average score of 90%, indicating a highly satisfactory user experience.

articleTitle: Forecasting Customer Baseline Load Based on Similar Electricity Usage Patterns
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: In incentive-based demand response programs, compensation is calculated and paid to participants who adjust their electricity usage as requested. This is based on the difference between the Customer Baseline Load (CBL) the estimated electricity usage without participating in the program and the actual load during the event. Accurate CBL calculation ensures fair compensation, incentivizing participation. This research develops a model to forecast CBL using K-Means clustering, incorporating Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) as a distance metric. The centroid from each cluster represents the CBL for individual customers within the cluster. This approach is compared to the traditional "Max 4/5" method. Results show the centroid-based CBL calculation aligns more closely with actual electricity usage, with a relative root mean square error (RRMSE) of 0.175 compared to 0.312 for the Max 4/5 method.

articleTitle: Aerial Base Station Positioning Evaluation for UAV-assisted Het-Nets
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The requirements presented by the new application scenarios and use-cases for modern wireless networks have led to the increasingly heterogeneous types of communication nodes with various density. The implementation of unmanned aerial vechile (UAV) based aerial base stations (ABSs) into the current and upcoming heterogenous networks (Het-Nets) has a growing importance for research in the field. Determining the positioning of the ABS is a crucial aspect in UAV-assisted networks. This paper presents an evaluation of the throughput for different positions (random, center, and the four edges of the UAV operational region) for the ABS within an UAV-assisted Het-Net. Based on the system throughput, the best ABS position is empirically determined and the gain provided by the ABS in comparison to the traditional Het-Net, is assessed. System throughput of up to 190 Mbps is achieved, which is nearly 3 times higher than that in the alternative case.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Screen Printed Carbon Paste Electrochemical Sensors for Lab on a Chip
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: In this research, screen printed electrochemical sensor of lab on a chip was designed and fabricated by screen printing. The chip was designed with integrated digital microfluidic microchip and electrochemical sensors on single plate substrate. For the design, the chip consist of H-junction EWOD digital microfluidics microchip for various biochemical analyses with merging buffer reagent and analyze droplets and an electrochemical detector at the end of H-junction EWOD. Both parts were fabricated by screen printed technique for supporting low cost manufacturing process. The EWOD microchip consists of silver paste for electrodes layers and PDMS for dielectric and Teflon<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> AF hydrophobic layers. Three electrodes of electrochemical sensor consist of a carbon paste working electrode and a carbon paste counter electrode, and silver/silver chloride paste reference electrode for rapid analysis with minimal reagent consumption. In experimental study, the electrochemical sensor combine with EWOD microchip was tested to analyst for hydrogen peroxide for rapid analysis with minimal reagent consumption.

articleTitle: UNet-Stream for Segmentation of Ultrasound Images of Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Detecting breast cancer at early stages is vital for effective treatment, planning and improvement of the patient outcomes. UNet is a popular deep learning (DL) model applicable to the segmentation of a variety of medical images. This study presents a numerical analysis of UNet applied to segmenting breast ultrasound (US) images. 286 breast US images collected and labeled by Thammasat University Hospital are pre-processed and augmented. The selected variant of the UNet model is based on the recent UNet architectures principles [1], combined with the stream line portrait (SLP) of the Ultrasound (US) image called the UNet-Stream. The weights are initialized using the Glorot-Uniform weight procedure. The model achieves promising results with a validation accuracy of 98.55%. The F1 score is 94.725%, Intersection over Union (IoU) is 89.089%, precision is 95.425%, specificity is 99.245%, and recall is 95.227%.

articleTitle: Broadband Unidirectional Vivaldi Antenna for Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a broadband Vivaldi antenna intended for radar systems operating across the 2-6 GHz frequency range. The antenna design employs an optimized corrugated Vivaldi antenna and a coaxial feed structure to ensure wideband performance. A 50-ohm N-type connector is integrated for efficient signal transmission between the antenna feed, transmitter, and receiver, minimizing reflection losses and enhancing overall system efficiency. Measurements show that the antenna achieves Half-Power Beamwidth (HPBW) values of 100° for the xz-plane and 80° for the yz-plane at 2.45 GHz, 80° for the xz-plane and 60° for the yz-plane at 3.5 GHz, and 80° for the xz-plane and 40° for the yz-plane at 5.5 GHz. Additionally, the antenna gains increase with frequency, reaching 6.60 dBi at 2.45 GHz, 8.34 dBi at 3.5 GHz, and 11.74 dBi at 5.5 GHz. The proposed Vivaldi antenna configuration is particularly suited for radar applications that require multi-band operation, facilitating the detection and tracking of various target sizes and distances. By covering a broad bandwidth, this design improves radar system performance, particularly in frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar environments, enabling robust target detection in diverse operating conditions.

articleTitle: Design Optimization Control of Blower in Coffee Roasting Process with Fuzzy Logic Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Coffee is a key commodity in Indonesia's plantation sector, where the quality of coffee flavor is influenced by the beans (60%) and the roasting process (30%) [1]. To improve the quality, a coffee roaster with controlled temperature and stable process is used. It has a closed combustion system with a 25 cm diameter tube and a capacity of 500 grams of green beans. Temperature stability is maintained by controlling the speed of the heat dissipation blower and the gas path through an automatic valve based on a threshold value [2]. The system uses K-type thermocouple sensors to detect temperature, with inputs in the form of error and integral error. Fuzzy logic control regulates the speed of the adaptive blower motor based on temperature changes. The sensor output generates an 8-bit PWM value through a zero crossing detector to adjust the speed of the AC blower motor. For example, at a temperature error of -10 and integral error of -1000, the system generates a value of 817.6 which is converted to 67% to adjust the blower motor speed. The gas valve is set with a threshold value of ±1℃. The results show that the system is more efficient with a reduction in excess oscillation.

articleTitle: MESIAS: A Web Application for Evaluating Ethical and Security Considerations in AI Project Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence has revolutionized various sectors, but its successful implementation encounters significant security, ethics, and reliability challenges. This study presents a web-based tool addressing security and ethical considerations across various phases of AI projects. The platform features a virtual assistant and a best practices repository, which aids in project evaluation and offers personalized recommendations for risk mitigation. The application was validated through a case study involving 20 professionals from a technology consulting firm in Lima, Peru, who participated in a satisfaction survey during its preliminary phase. The results indicate a high acceptance level, with an average overall satisfaction score of 4.48, suggesting a favorable impact of the tool. This study establishes a foundation for comparative evaluations in future system implementation phases.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality for Anxiety Reduction in Individuals with Autism
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is often associated with heightened anxiety levels, particularly in novel or unpredictable environments. Virtual Reality (VR) offers a promising tool for addressing anxiety through controlled, immersive environments. This paper explores the application of VR as a therapeutic tool to reduce anxiety in individuals with autism. We discuss the design and implementation of various VR environments, the methodologies employed, and the results obtained from clinical trials. Key findings include significant anxiety reduction, increased engagement, and positive feedback from both participants and caregivers.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Sensor for Lab on a Chip with Conductive ink by Screen Printing
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research focuses on studying electrochemical electrodes by applying screen printing technology to create an innovative printing approach. The material used is a graphene-carbon plate, and the electrochemical electrode is designed with three primary electrodes: a working electrode for graphene-carbon deposition, a counter electrode for graphene-carbon deposition, and a reference electrode for silver/silver chloride deposition to achieve high-performance analysis. The EWOD microchip consists of a silver paste for the electrode layer and PDMS for the dielectric layer. The three electrodes are printed on the H-pattern circuit layout. The EWOD system is utilized for combining reagent buffers and analytical droplets. In terms of analysis, the experiments varied the concentration of the analyte at 10, 50, 100, 250, and 500 micromolar using cyclic voltammetry. The test substance with the highest electrochemical properties was identified using SPGE (Screen-Printed Graphene Electrode) for electrochemical detection. The analysis focused on detecting potassium hexacyanoferrate (K4Fe(CN)6) to evaluate the electrochemical properties.

articleTitle: The Optimal Real-time Environment with IoT Technologies for Hemp Propagation
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The world faced poverty from 2020 to 2023 due to COVID-19, increasing the need for medicines and herbs for disease prevention and treatment. Reviving the economy and generating income for the population became a global policy. Thailand's policy includes cultivating hemp as a controlled herb for medical and commercial purposes. This cultivation requires permission and THC certification of less than 1 percent, with seeds being difficult to obtain and expensive, costing 200 baht per seed and having a germination rate of less than 60 percent. Selecting parent plants from seeds for stem cuttings is a solution for farmers. The Internet of Things system developed by RMUTL Smart Farm, Faculty of Engineering, Rajamangala University of Technology Lanna, is used for irrigation and climate monitoring in collaboration with community enterprises in Lamphun Province. IoT technology aids in remote control and detection, reducing labor costs and increasing efficiency to achieve quality output, generating income for community enterprises over the past two years. The initial planting involves propagation to ensure complete root development. This research aims to combine the advantages of traditional methods with advanced IoT technology for environmental control in a nursery chamber during the pre-adventitious root formation period without homogeneous plants.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Diplexer without Internal Coupling Iris
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research proposes a dielectric resonator diplexer with single-mode capabilities. The proposed single-mode dielectric resonator diplexer comprised a rectangular dielectric resonator with a central hole, which helps to shift the spurious frequency away from the fundamental frequency. The external Qe of the resonator is configured using an I/O coaxial probe, and the internal coupling between two resonators is adjustable without the need for irises. The diplexer circuit, modeled as a second-order design, was simulated using HFSS software to operate at Rx and Tx at 1.95 GHz and 2.14 GHz, achieving a 3-dB fractional bandwidth of 3.59% (70 MHz). The passband of the insertion loss is less than 0.04 dB for both channels, and a return loss exceeds 20 dB for the passband.

articleTitle: Recapping Knowledge and Practice: Knowledge Transfer in Child Protection Specialist Through Community of Practice in Faith-Based Organization
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study focuses on recapping the key knowledge and practices of Child Protection Specialists (CPS) in a faith-based organization (FBO) in Thailand to facilitate knowledge sharing through a Community of Practice (CoP). The goal is to identify the essential knowledge needed for CPS and explore how CoP can help organize and share this information. Using the Theory of Change (ToC) framework, the study looks at the challenges in child protection, especially the role of human resources in achieving success. Through methods like document analysis, expert interviews, and workshops, the study identifies key laws and practices related to child protection. The findings highlight the need for clear and structured ways to share knowledge to improve the skills of non-CPS staff. The study also shows how using the CoP digital platform can help store and share knowledge within the organization, strengthening child protection efforts

articleTitle: Enhancing the Production of White Charcoal and Syngas from a Stove with an IoT Airflow Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The aim of this study is to improve the production of white charcoal and syngas using a stove equipped with an IoT airflow controller. The airflow regulation system for a gasification furnace including a double-burner, utilized for syngas production alongside white charcoal. The temperature range for a double-burner gasification furnace, utilizing the prescribed IoT air flow control system, is between 800 and 1,250 °C. The gasification reaction at the stove's exterior generates syngas, while the pyrolysis process at the stove's core produces white charcoal. The experimental air flow rate ratio ranged from 2.5 to 4 m/s to examine the yield of syngas and the characteristics of white charcoal derived from rice husk. The implementation of an IoT air flow control system revealed that the air flow rate could be adjusted and the furnace temperature could be continually modulated in response to variations in reactivity within the furnace.

articleTitle: Predicting Public Transport Passenger Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study compares five predictive models for passenger demand at the Lima Metro's Line 1 stations: Prophet, Linear Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree, and AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA). The analysis utilizes a dataset extracted from the OSITRAN website, which includes information on the number of passengers who used the metro at various stations during specific times. Data was collected from July 1 to July 7, 2024, between 5 a.m. and 11 p.m., covering all 26 metro stations. The evaluation metrics used in this study are Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The results indicate that Prophet achieved the highest scores across all three metrics, establishing it as a viable solution compared to the other models analyzed.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Estimation Through Vascular Contraction Signal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Diabetes is a critical health concern globally, as it impacts overall health and serves as a precursor to other conditions. Regular monitoring of blood glucose levels is essential for effective diabetes management. However, current glucose monitoring devices are invasive, leading to tissue damage, pain, and an increased risk of infection. This paper presents a continued study on the development of a non-invasive blood glucose estimation system. Using transmitting light energy in the near-infrared wavelength and near-red wavelength to detect and record PPG signals using an ESP32 microcontroller with a MAX30102 sensor. The MAX30102 sensor can transmit and receive light in red (660 nm) and near-infrared (880 nm) and measure on the fingertip. PPG signals are then analyzed for their prominent features, revealing the relationship between blood glucose levels and the most prominent features, namely root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) power in the high frequency range (PowHF) and ratio of low frequency range to high frequency range (LF/HF) of the red wavelength. Subsequently, these features were utilized using Multiple regression equations, with one and two variables. Each of 10 Subject participated experimental session lasts approximately 2 hours and 35 minutes. Finally, the best-performing model is the two-variable regression equation model for data from the second segment after signal filtering consisting of Glucose, RMSSD and PowHF of the red wavelength, achieving an accuracy of 89.86%.

articleTitle: Detection of Malnutrition in Children Under 5 Years of Old Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for the early detection of childhood malnutrition. The architectures analyzed include ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B4, VGG16, and AlexNet, selected for their demonstrated effectiveness in image classification tasks. Images were categorized into three classes—normal, at risk of malnutrition, and severely malnourished—and underwent preprocessing steps such as resizing, flipping, zooming, and face detection using MTCNN. The evaluation employed metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, with ResNet-50 emerging as the most effective model, achieving an accuracy of 92%. Based on these findings, this study explores the potential application of ResNet-50 in mobile solutions to provide accessible and practical tools for malnutrition detection in resource-limited settings.

articleTitle: Negative Binomial Regression Model for Predicting the Number of Tourists in National Parks of Thailand
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This article examines the use of count data models to predict the number of tourists visiting Thailand’s national parks. The dataset, encompassing observations from 2016 to 2022 across 146 national parks, exhibits characteristics such as discreteness, over dispersion, and non-negative integer values. Two models— Poisson (POI), and Negative Binomial (NB)—were compared to identify the most effective approach for modeling and prediction. Model evaluation metrics, including the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and log-likelihood, were employed. Results demonstrate that the Negative Binomial regression model best captures the data’s overdispersion compared to the POI model. The NB model achieved the lowest AIC and highest log-likelihood, affirming its superior performance for this application. Our findings underscore the NB model’s utility in predicting tourism-related count data and suggest its broader applicability to other domains characterized by overdispersed count data.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Broken Gate TFET and its RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: In this study, we introduce a novel Broken-Gate Tunnel Field-Effect Transistor (BG-TFET) architecture based on silicon. The structure has been refined and analytically characterized. The device showcases an enhanced subthreshold slope (SS) of 19 mV/dec, minimal bidirectional current, and ON-current values on par with contemporary designs of similar dimensions. The findings of the device parameters are corroborated through the simulations of SILVACO employing the methodology of Nonlocal tunneling.

articleTitle: A Memristor-Based VCO for Switching-Mode PLL System
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: In this paper, a memristor-based sinusoidal VCO using a single OTA with dual-current output is presented. The Resistance-Controlled-Gain (RCG) property of the OTA is used for accomplishing memristance independent oscillation condition. The proposed design operates in a frequency range between 20 MHz and 30 MHz. It can be integrated with a memristor-based phase-frequency-detector to introduce a memristor-based phase-locked-loop system with low area and power consumption valid for many biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Puma Optimizer Algorithm for Optimization Problems
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper proposes an enhanced Puma Optimizer Algorithm for solving optimization problems. The Rao Algorithm is incorporated and refined within the exploration phase of the Puma Optimizer, incorporating novel procedures to improve position updates. The proposed algorithm is evaluated on six benchmark functions. An evaluation results show in comparison to Differential Evolution (DE), Intersection Mutation Differential Evolution (IMDE), the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), and the Sand Cat Swarm Optimization Algorithm (SCSO). Computational results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves optimal solutions for two of the six benchmark functions. Furthermore, it consistently outperforms the other four algorithms across the test suite. These findings highlight the potential for further advancements in the Puma Optimizer and demonstrate its effectiveness in addressing continuous step functions, multimodal functions, and discontinuous step functions, achieving performance that is competitive with or surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Developing a Social Skills-Based Framework to Foster Workforce Resilience and Adaptability
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: In today’s rapidly changing in technology, organizations face immense pressure to adapt and innovate to ensure long-term success, making workforce resilience and adaptability critical priorities. Despite the strategic importance of these traits, many organizations, including office of Chiang Mai University, struggle to bridge the gap between competency development and sustained behavioral change, largely due to fixed mindsets and limited collaboration. This study addresses these challenges by leveraging theoretical frameworks such as growth mindset, icebreaking activities, and design thinking to foster adaptability, teamwork, and innovation. The objective is to develop and implement a social skills-based framework that drives meaningful behavioral transformation. Using a structured methodology, this research conducted workshops emphasizing key attributes like adaptability and teamwork, followed by pre- and post-training assessments. Results demonstrated significant behavioral improvements in trust, teamwork, and self-development, validating the framework’s potential to transform organizational culture and enhance workforce performance.

Author Keywords: social Skills Development and behavioral Change

articleTitle: Digital Transformation in Hospitals: The Impact of RFID on Workflow and Staff Productivity
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The integration of Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology into hospital workflows has proven to enhance operational efficiency and improve resource management. This study examines the impact of RFID on key hospital metrics, including tag reading rate, equipment retrieval time, inventory accuracy, and staff productivity. Results indicate that the RFID system achieved a tag reading rate of 11 tags per second, significantly reducing equipment retrieval time by 30.1%. Additionally, RFID contributed to a 24.6% reduction in stock shortages and a 14.9% decrease in overstocking, improving inventory accuracy to 98%. Furthermore, staff productivity increased by 20.8%, as healthcare professionals were able to dedicate more time to patient care due to reduced time spent on administrative tasks. These findings highlight the substantial benefits of RFID technology in streamlining hospital operations, enhancing resource management, and improving overall patient care, positioning RFID as a valuable tool for healthcare institutions seeking to optimize their workflows and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Proposing ChatGPT as a Transformative Tool for Enhancing ESL Speaking and Listening Skills: Bridging Research Gaps in Thai Education
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The development of speaking and listening skills remains a significant challenge in English as a Second Language (ESL) education, particularly in non-native English-speaking contexts such as Thailand. Traditional tools and methods often fail to provide personalized, real-time conversational practice, leaving gaps in learners’ communicative competence. This paper explores ChatGPT, a conversational AI, as a potential solution to these challenges. By conducting a comprehensive review of existing tools and identifying research gaps, this study proposes a conceptual framework for integrating ChatGPT into ESL education, particularly for Thai students at Chiang Rai Rajabhat University (CRRU). This framework highlights how ChatGPT’s interactive capabilities can address cultural and linguistic barriers, enhance learner engagement, and provide scalable solutions for improving speaking and listening skills. The paper concludes with recommendations for future research and practical implications for educators.

articleTitle: Topology Study of Urban Railway Networks in Bangkok Metropolitan Area for Route and Distance-based Centralities
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The three main centralities of rapid transit and suburban rail networks, closeness, betweenness, and information, which are based on route and distance, were considered useful for measuring the critical stations in a railway network. Therefore, considering the Bangkok metropolitan area that still continually expands its railway network, this study analysed the topological changes of urban railways anticipated from 2024 to 2028. The results can help operators identify and analyse critical stations, which have an extensive effect on the network if they are disrupted or cut off and must be managed for protection and routine preventive maintenance.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Electrochemical Sensor of Lab on a Chip for Depressive Substance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study developed and evaluated a screen-printed electrowetting on dielectric (EWOD) microchip specifically designed for analyzing depression-related substances. The microchip features a two-part T-junction EWOD structure composed of a silver electrode layer and a dielectric layer made of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Positioned at the end of the T-junction, the integrated electrochemical sensor includes three detectors: a screen-printed graphene/carbon working electrode, a counter electrode, and a silver/silver chloride reference electrode. Both electrode layers were fabricated through a layer-by-layer screen-printing technique, while the PDMS layer was created using spin coating. The device employs cyclic voltammetry (CV) to detect electroactive compounds associated with depression. Results indicate that this electrochemical sensor demonstrates significant potential for precise and reliable analysis of depressive substances.

articleTitle: Customer Knowledge Management Model to enhance Chinese customer shopping experience in Chiang Mai Shopping Mall
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Chinese customers are fast becoming a key contributor in the Thailand's tourism industry. As the second favorite tourist destination for Chinese in Thailand, it is necessary to study their shopping experience in Chiang Mai Shopping malls. This study used Customer Knowledge Management(CKM) to help gain a deeper understanding of Chinese customers' shopping experience at Chiang Mai shopping malls. Identified the existing problems during their shopping, referred to other successful Chinese shopping malls in improving customer experience, combined with experiential marketing Kano Model, proposed and validated strategies to satisfy customers. Finally, the feasibility and operability of these strategies were verified through communication with the biggest shopping mall in Chiang Mai.

articleTitle: The Design of the Conversational Chatbot Using Facebook Messenger to Support Patient Services: A Case Study of a Dental Clinic, University of Phayao
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research aims to design a conversational chatbot, facebook messenger, to provide dental services at the Dental Hospital, Faculty of Dentistry, University of Phayao. facebook messenger will be used to deliver dental service information and reduce delays in inquiries. The researchers developed a chatbot system to offer consultation and dental treatment information. The chatbot service is available 24 hours daily, ensuring they receive the necessary information promptly. Additionally, the researchers designed infographic images to be used alongside chatbot text messages, making the responses more straightforward to understand. The study found that infographics with chatbot messages made the conversations more engaging. Users were most satisfied with the clarity of information provided by the chatbot with infographics, with an average rating of 4.93. The conversational chatbot was followed by the chatbot's ability to make conversations more interesting, with an average rating of 4.86, and overall satisfaction with using the chatbot with infographics, with an average rating of 4.85. The results indicate that users are delighted with the chatbot service system.

articleTitle: Slotted Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna for 2.4 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This work proposes a slotted rectangular-microstrip patch antenna for Wi-Fi band (2.4 GHz). The antenna was designed using CST Microwave Studio, which is utilized for designing a slotted rectangular-microstrip patch antenna with a simple design structure, utilizing an inset feed for signal feeding. The slotted line is positioned adjacent to the microstrip patch antenna, which helps in adjusting the loss and achieving a good bandwidth simultaneously. Through the design and simulation, it was found that achieving a return loss of nearly 22 dB and a VSWR of 1 at 2.4 GHz, with a bandwidth around 130 MHz. These designs can be applied to wireless internet applications.

articleTitle: An Augmented Reality-Based Hazardous Waste Management Learning System : A Case Study of Elementary School Students in Chiang Rai Province
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research applies augmented reality (AR) technology to enhance learning and understanding of hazardous waste separation, while raising awareness of the dangers, particularly primary school students. These students, as users, often dispose of waste without knowing whether it is hazardous or not, and they lack an understanding of proper waste separation and disposal processes. Recognizing this issue, the researchers aim to develop AR-based educational media for waste management, using animation to convey knowledge and content in a virtual environment. The goal is to align the educational content with the learners' needs while engaging them effectively. This study also evaluates the efficiency of the developed learning system by collecting data from actual users to assess both the effectiveness of the media and user satisfaction, providing insights for further development.

articleTitle: Satisfaction Analysis of Data and Application Architecture in the Enterprise Blueprint of the Faculty of Dentistry, University of Phayao
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research aims to analyze the satisfaction of staff members at the Faculty of Dentistry, University of Phayao, regarding the use of application systems that support business processes, focusing on the data architecture and application architecture, as well as studying the technology architecture infrastructure that supports operational activities in the faculty. The study’s sample consisted of 75 staff members of the Faculty of Dentistry, using questionnaires to collect data on their satisfaction with application systems developed at the university level and those specifically designed for the faculty. Data analysis utilized descriptive statistics, including mean, standard deviation, and frequency analysis. The findings revealed that satisfaction with application systems at the university level highlighted the document management system’s mean score of 4.60 and the inventory management system’s mean score of 4.56 as the most satisfactory. Regarding application systems specifically developed for the Faculty of Dentistry, the room reservation and repair request systems were rated as the most acceptable, with a mean score of 4.59. Additionally, the study of technology architecture showed that the Faculty of Dentistry has a well-established infrastructure, including high-speed networks such as the UNINET system and wireless networks, as well as compliance with information security standards, such as the computer crime act and personal data protection act.
