Recommendations from the study include improving and further developing application systems to meet user needs better and expanding the coverage of technology infrastructure to support future operations effectively.

articleTitle: Development of Intelligent Medication Care Taker
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Currently, there is a significant number of elderly patients with chronic diseases or individuals who are unable to adequately care for themselves seeking medical treatment. Many of these patients often fail to follow or neglect medication instructions, leading to deviations from expected treatment outcomes or even failure in patient recovery. The primary reason for non-compliance with medical treatment is the forgetfulness of patients in taking their prescribed medication. This paper aims to present the practical application and testing of the Intelligent Medication Care Taker, a device designed to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of medical treatment management for both healthcare providers and patients. The goal of this research is to reduce the burden on caregivers and help resolve the issue of patients forgetting to take their medication on time. The main structure of the Intelligent Medication Care Taker is constructed from acrylic, with a Raspberry Pi 4 serving as the central controller for all functions, including video conferencing, voice reminders, and electric door locks. When it is time for the patient to take their medication, an alarm sounds, and the electric lock automatically unlocks the compartment door, allowing the patient access to their medication. For video calls, the doctor initiates the meeting, and the patient can join the session by pressing a button to communicate with the doctor. This system supports telemedicine consultations, enabling patients to receive medical care while allowing doctors to monitor the patient's condition conveniently from home, thus reducing the need for travel and mitigating other barriers to visiting hospitals or clinics. Appointments can also be scheduled conveniently through a website accessible via the device’s screen. Ultimately, this research aims to reduce the occurrence of missed doses and improve the effectiveness of treatment, thus enhancing patient health outcomes.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Color Restoration of Faded Historical Paintings
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The degradation of color in historical paintings poses a significant challenge to art preservation, diminishing the vibrancy and authenticity of masterpieces over time. This paper explores the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to revolutionize color restoration in historical artworks. By leveraging advanced machine learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs), AI systems can analyze faded paintings and reconstruct their original hues with unprecedented precision. Using large datasets of high-resolution images, these algorithms learn patterns of pigment degradation and stylistic nuances inherent to specific artists or periods. The study highlights how AI models, trained on multispectral and hyperspectral imaging data, can infer the original color schemes by detecting remnants of pigments invisible to the naked eye. Moreover, AI-driven simulations offer insights into artistic intent and historical contexts, enabling restorers to make informed decisions. This interdisciplinary approach merges art history, chemistry, and computer science, fostering a new era of cultural heritage preservation. The findings underscore AI's transformative role in safeguarding the visual integrity of humanity's artistic legacy while maintaining the ethical considerations of artistic authenticity and conservation standards.

articleTitle: Shop Floor Productivity Improvement in Original Equipment Manufacturer Company Using ODOO ERP
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is one solution for starting a new business in this era due to the difficulties of managing the supply chain, manufacturing processes, and high startup costs. However, the majority of Thai industries operate relying on human labor and basic mechanization, leading to inefficiencies. This paper presents the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems using Odoo, an open-source ERP software, to address these inefficiencies. This research focuses on implementing the Odoo ERP system on the shop floor of an OEM company, addressing challenges in the planning and production departments. The current business process (As-is process) contains several problems. Through gap analysis and customization of the Odoo ERP modules, the system provides streamlined processes according to the new planning and production business process (To-be process), reducing delays and providing real-time access to information. The implementation results show that the system supports OEM company on the shop floor process and enhances overall productivity.

articleTitle: Knowledge-based Graph Exploration Analysis on Customer’s Preference of Insurance Services
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: With the increasing number of Chinese students in Thailand, the demand for insurance services from these students has gradually shown diversity and personalized characteristics. However, the current research on the insurance demand of overseas students is relatively insufficient. Based on text analysis and knowledge graph technology, this study focuses on the needs and preferences of Chinese students in Thailand in terms of insurance choices, and presents the research results in a visual form. The researchers collected chat history content of some target groups, as well as public discussion data on social media platforms and forums frequently used by Chinese students in Thailand. The researchers used the text analysis method to extract high-frequency keywords related to international student insurance, and carried out sentiment analysis to obtain the main concerns of current international students in insurance selection. Then, a knowledge graph centered on insurance demand is constructed to visualize key nodes and relationships such as insurance categories, budget preferences, and demand characteristics.

articleTitle: Perspectives of Mass Media Professionals on AI Adoption in Thailand's News Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the news industry has brought significant changes to the way news is produced. While AI has proven its ability to improve efficiency and automate repetitive tasks, questions about its reliability, emotional connection with audiences, and ability to adapt to sensitive or complex reporting remain unresolved. This study explores how media professionals perceive the role of AI in news production, focusing on its cost-effectiveness, efficiency, limitations, and reliability. The research, conducted with a Thai news agency as a case study, involved in-depth interviews with 11 industry experts who shared their experiences and views on the use of AI in journalism. The results showed that AI excels at handling repetitive tasks and delivering news quickly and consistently, boosting newsroom efficiency. However, experts pointed out its inability to convey emotions, understand context, or adapt to real-time changes, making it less suitable for in-depth or sensitive reporting. Despite these limitations, 90.9% of respondents acknowledged that AI effectively enhances productivity for routine tasks. Concerns about audience trust and the high initial costs of adopting AI were also frequently mentioned. While AI is a valuable tool for improving operational efficiency in newsrooms, it cannot replace human journalists in areas that demand emotional intelligence and contextual understanding. The study concludes that a balanced integration of AI and human roles is essential, with AI taking on repetitive tasks and journalists focusing on maintaining trust, depth, and quality in reporting. This approach ensures the responsible use of AI to meet the evolving demands of the media industry.

articleTitle: Pedagogical Benchmark for Smart Grid Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper presents the comprehensive design and implementation of a Power Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHIL) educational benchmark system for smart grid scenarios. The system features an advanced electrical cabinet incorporating multiple bidirectional DC-DC converter legs with a common 100kW grid connection interface, a back-to-back front-end grid-side converter with galvanic isolation, and an internal DC link. The hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) architecture enables real-time control and monitoring through MATLAB-Simulink integration, supported by a real-time target system. The benchmark demonstrates various DC microgrid configurations through four operational scenarios: independent converter control, microDC network emulation, battery-to-battery energy transfer, and renewable energy integration. Operating at high efficiency (>95%), the system serves as a power electronics educational platform at the University of Lyon 1, providing hands-on experience with smart grid technologies. The design emphasizes energy-efficient operation through regenerative capabilities between DC legs, while maintaining robust safety protocols for both equipment and users. This educational benchmark system bridges the gap between theoretical power electronics education and practical smart grid implementation, offering a versatile platform for studying real-time control strategies and renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: Examine and Assess the Influence of Content Development on Xiaohongshu Platform for Brand Interaction: An In-depth Analysis of a Minor Stationery Corporation's Strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper takes the small stationery brand of XiaoHongshu platform as the research object, and discusses the influence of its content marketing on brand communication. Through the combination of quantitative and qualitative methods, 400 "notes" from 20 leading small stationery brands were analyzed, considering external factors such as release timing, market competition, and product popularity, and the characteristics of high-quality and low-quality notes and their communication effects were summarized. The study also takes into account social behavior factors, such as the use of Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs). These factors can significantly influence user engagement and brand perception. The study found that high-quality notes are generally outstanding in cover design, title relevance, content graphic combination and hashtag use, and are more inclined to use video (62% of high-quality notes), and significantly improve user interaction (average engagement volume 19,763). In addition, "Product display" and "product details introduction" accounted for the highest proportion of topics in notes, at 42.5% and 36%, respectively. Statistical analysis yielded χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>= 67.5, p<0.05. χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>= 67.5 shows that there is a significant difference between video notes and graphic notes in introducing product details. p<0.05 indicates that video notes dominate the introduction of product details. This paper further proposes strategies to optimize content marketing, including enhancing brand style unity, strengthening product detail display and increasing the proportion of video content, so as to help small stationery brands achieve brand communication goals more efficiently.

articleTitle: Enhancing Student Support Services for Chinese International Students in Chiang Mai University
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Currently, among the ever-increasing number of international students studying in Thai universities, Chinese students occupy the largest proportion. Due to the particularity of Chinese students, additional support services were required. In addition, targeted student support services will help the institution to better support Chinese students in their study life and enhance the institution's internationalization. Most studies have focused on general support services rather than targeted services. This study explores the current international student support services and additional service requires of educators and Chinese graduate students in College of Arts, Media and Technology in Chiang Mai University. The jobs to be done theory was used in this study. The results of this study show multiple desired outcomes in each job steps that can help university to create tailored student support services according to the distinct demand of educators and Chinese students.

articleTitle: Influencing Factors of DOUYIN Influencer in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper explores the key factors for the success of Chinese DOUYIN influencers in Thailand. By analyzing the comments of Chinese users on the DOUYIN platform on influencer videos, and using frequency and factor analysis methods and tools, high-frequency keywords are identified through analysis. The paper highlights how fan engagement, influencer professionalism and content innovation play a key role in helping influencers succeed. Insights from the study provide practical implications for influencers and marketers aiming to maximize their reach in the Thai market through China DOUYIN. The 3,000 comments has been collected from the first 10 best influencer's customer response, during 2023 between October and December using the BAZHUAYU data collection tool. This study identified the factors needed to become a DOUYIN influencer on Thai-related topics, and the results will provide valuable references and creative new ideas for content creators who want to produce Thai-related topics on the DOUYIN platform.

articleTitle: Designing a Gamified Mixed Reality System for Social Skills Development in High-Functioning Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study examines the integration of Mixed Reality (MR) systems with gamification to enhance social skills in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder. Designed to provide a safe and engaging environment, the system incorporates gamified elements to sustain motivation and facilitate learning. Evaluated with five participants aged 6–10 years from the Banprajan Child Center, the intervention demonstrated significant improvements in social interaction, emotion recognition, and communication skills for some participants, while usability testing revealed high satisfaction among therapists. Despite promising results, limitations such as a small sample size and accessibility challenges underscore the need for future research to scale the system, integrate adaptive AI mechanisms, and assess long-term impact. This study offers a foundation for innovative, personalized interventions addressing the needs of children with ASD.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Deep Learning-based Person Re-identification Across Multi-Cameras
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Surveillance systems play an essential role in enhancing security and ensuring safety within society. Public spaces and critical areas are commonly monitored through multi-camera networks for tracking individuals in real-time to enable quick responses to potential security threats. However, variations in lighting, camera angles, and occlusions pose significant challenges to the process of recognizing individuals across multiple camera views. This research proposes a Person Re-Identification (Re-ID) with deep learning and feature extraction method to improve the accuracy of individual matching and identification despite these challenges. This research encompasses multiple neural network topologies, such as ResNet50, ResNet101, and OSNet architectures with traditional computer vision methodologies such as Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) to examine the body part weighting coefficients and feature selection mechanisms. The results demonstrated that integrating dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis (PCA) coupled with semantic segmentation techniques yields statistically significant improvements in re-identification accuracy. The ResNet101 architecture emerges as the superior methodology, achieving performance with a Rank-1 accuracy of 0.88 and mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.94 on the test dataset.

articleTitle: Ecotourism-Based Artificial Intelligence: Case Study in Bekasi Regency
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in ecotourism has emerged as a transformative approach to achieving sustainable tourism goals. By leveraging AI technologies, tourism destinations can enhance operational efficiency, personalize visitor experiences, and foster environmental conservation. This study examines the implementation of an AI-powered application in Bekasi Regency, Indonesia, a region known for its rich natural and cultural heritage. Key features such as real-time monitoring, AI-driven recommendations, and interactive mapping were developed to address ecological challenges while promoting sustainable tourism practices. The study also discusses the implications of data privacy, algorithmic bias, and social inclusivity in adopting AI-driven solutions. It demonstrates how technology can provide a balanced approach to advancing ecotourism while supporting local communities.

articleTitle: Detecting Implicit Subjects in Text
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study presents a rule-based approach for detecting and replacing implicit subjects in text, focusing on business process descriptions. Implicit subjects, commonly omitted in natural language, pose challenges for tasks like comparison and extraction. I propose a pipeline to identify instances of implicit subjects, extract candidates from context, and insert the correct subject into sentences. Evaluation highlights areas for improvement, including expanding subject classes, refining occurrence and similarity filters, and integrating generative AI for enhanced accuracy. This framework contributes to natural language understanding, particularly in business process contexts.

articleTitle: Does Data Balancing Play an Important Role in Classifying Road Accident Severity in Thailand?
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Unlike many studies that focus on binary classification, this study uniquely addresses road crash severity (RCS) classification in Thailand using three categories. A dataset of 31,817 cases collected between 2021 and 2022 was analyzed using nine features and four classifiers: Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR), Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). The severity of the road crash was divided into three classes: no injuries or fatalities (46.47%), injuries (42.97%), and fatalities (10.56%). To mitigate class imbalance, the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) was implemented. Subsequently, all classification performances were improved, especially in terms of the F1-G-Mean. Among four classifiers, LASSO and XGBoost showed the highest G-Mean of 0.6928 and sensitivity of 0.4877, respectively. RF presented the highest Fl-Score of 0.4359 and Fl-G-Mean of 0.4189. At α = 0.05, the Friedman test confirmed the significant performance differences between imbalanced and SMOTE scenarios. However, the overall improvements were moderate, suggesting that the data balancing alone is insufficient for optimal performance. These findings highlight the critical role of addressing class imbalance in improving classification reliability while emphasizing the need for additional techniques, such as advanced resampling, feature engineering, and hyperparameter tuning, to further enhance model performance. The study provides valuable insights for developing data-driven strategies to reduce road accident impacts in Thailand.

articleTitle: YOLOv8 for Personal Device Screen Detection to Preserve Data Privacy: Enhancing Security Measures in Real-Time Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: In public and semi-public environments, personal device usage often exposes sensitive information, presenting a challenge to user privacy when such data is captured by surveillance systems. This study investigates the application of YOLOv8, an advanced object detection model, to identify and obscure personal electronic device screens, particularly mobile phones, in CCTV footage. Utilizing real-time blurring with a Gaussian kernel, this approach ensures that sensitive information displayed on these devices remains unreadable in video footage. The study aims to address the following research questions: (1) Each version of YOLOv8 varies in its effectiveness for detecting and identifying mobile device screens? (2) What level of Gaussian blurring is sufficient to obscure sensitive information without compromising processing efficiency? Experimental results demonstrate that YOLOv8m consistently excels, particularly in precision and mAP50, making it the ideal choice for applications where high accuracy is essential. Meanwhile, YOLOv8n, as the smallest model, delivers promising outcomes in terms of processing speed. Additionally, a 35x35 Gaussian kernel achieves an optimal balance between privacy protection and computational efficiency. These findings support the feasibility of integrating YOLOv8-based real-time blurring into surveillance systems, providing a robust solution for privacy protection in high-risk surveillance areas.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Strategies for Enhancing User Engagement in Play-to-Earn Games: Segmentation, Privilege Assignment Optimization, and Redemption Behavior Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study examines user behavior within the rapidly evolving Play-to-Earn (P2E) gaming market, focusing on challenges related to user retention, engagement, and monetization. The research question is what factors drive user engagement and redemption behavior in P2E games? Through a comprehensive methodology, we analyze data from a P2E platform to segment users, optimize privilege assignment timing, uncover behavioral patterns, and predict redemption behaviors. This approach integrates Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) analysis, data visualization, anomaly detection, clustering, and machine learning models. Key findings highlight distinct user segments based on engagement levels, ideal times for privilege assignment, and a model predicting redemption behavior. The insights provided offer game developers and marketers practical strategies to enhance user experience and boost platform performance in the competitive P2E landscape.

articleTitle: Harnessing AI for Agriculture: Applying Deep Learning Approaches to Detect and Classify Native Thai Vegetables in Specific Areas of Thailand
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research applies deep learning to classify native Thai vegetables, focusing on ten species from Northern Thailand. Using a dataset of 2,400 images collected from Phayao Province, six Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models — MobileNetV1, MobileNetV2, Xception, DenseNet, DenseNet121, and NASNetMobile—were evaluated for performance, with MobileNetV1 achieving the highest accuracy at 98.50%. Its lightweight design and efficiency make it ideal for mobile applications. A prototype app was developed to identify vegetables, share nutritional information, and suggest traditional recipes. This initiative promotes biodiversity conservation, healthier diets, and local economic growth. While challenges such as data collection and model refinement persist, this study highlights the potential of technology in preserving cultural heritage and supporting sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: Research on the Factors Influencing Consumer Purchase Intention in the Cross-Border Live Streaming E-commerce of the Cosmetics Industry from Thailand to China
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The advancement of international trade and cross-border e-commerce has facilitated greater access for consumers to acquire foreign products. Utilizing the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, this research investigates the determinants influencing Chinese consumers' purchasing behavior regarding Thai beauty products in the context of live e-commerce. The findings indicate that product safety, particularly concerning the safety of ingredients, is the primary concern for consumers. Furthermore, time-sensitive promotions and flash sales significantly enhance purchase intentions by instilling a sense of urgency. Thai hosts who are proficient in Chinese are more likely to foster consumer trust and improve brand communication, owing to their cultural alignment and linguistic advantages. While engaging content, such as product demonstrations and effect comparisons, can capture attention, its direct influence on purchasing decisions appears to be limited. The real-time interaction between hosts and audiences may augment perceived value and shopping satisfaction; however, its effect on purchase decisions remains ambiguous. In summary, perceived value is a critical factor in influencing purchase decisions, whereas perceived risk exerts a comparatively minor influence. Consequently, it is advisable for Thai beauty brands to cultivate trust by enhancing product quality, bolster competitiveness through strategic pricing, and facilitate effective communication by leveraging cultural compatibility. Although interactive and entertaining content can enrich the consumer experience, it should not serve as the primary strategy for driving purchase decisions.

articleTitle: Ant Colony Optimization for Multi-Label Correlation-based Feature Selection Method
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a new ant colony optimization for Multi-Label Correlation-Based Feature Selection (ACO-ML-CFS). This ACO performs a global search within the space of candidate features to identify an optimal subset. The selected feature subset is used by a Multi-Label k-Nearest Neighbors algorithm (ML-kNN), in this paper. The performance of ACO-ML-CFS is evaluated and compared with our previously works; Hill-Climbing algorithm for Multi-Label Correlation-Based Feature Selection (HC-ML-CFS) and Genetic algorithm for Multi-Label Correlation-Based Feature Selection (GA-ML-CFS) across four benchmark multi-label datasets.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Web System for the Automated Diagnosis of Phonological-Phonemic Disorders in Infants
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Early diagnosis of phonetic and phonological disorders in infants is crucial for their proper linguistic development. This paper presents a web-based system that automates the evaluation process by using deep learning models to analyze infant pronunciation. The system integrates an interactive video game that facilitates the collection of audios in a playful way. The goal is to improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, reducing subjectivity and evaluation time compared to traditional methods. The methodology includes the collection of audios from 3–5-year-old children, manual labeling of the data, and the use of deep neural networks to classify speech disorders into omission, distortion, substitution, and correct pronunciation. The results show that the Deep Neural Networks (DNN) model achieved an accuracy of approximately 95%, outperforming other algorithms evaluated. This system promises to be an effective tool to assist therapists in the early detection of phonetic problems, providing a faster and more accurate diagnosis.

articleTitle: Development and Integration of an Industrial Automation System based on the MQTT Protocol
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Industry 4.0 is a complex term used to describe the digital transformation of the manufacturing and industrial systems. It emphasizes connectivity, automation and real-time data integration. The Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol is one of the main driving forces behind this transformation. It is a lightweight, publish-subscribe messaging standard designed for efficient communications in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. The MQTT protocol provides seamless connectivity between diverse industrial devices, ensuring efficient data collection, transmission and integration with minimal network overhead. The MQTT gateways are among the key elements in the modern industrial automation applications and processes, but they also can bridge the legacy industrial systems and the advanced modern IIoT platforms. This is done by the translation of the traditional protocol data units into MQTT messages, which transforms the legacy systems into Industry 4.0-compliant solutions. The MQTT broker, acting as a central hub in the communication ecosystem, manages the message distribution among all connected devices, ensuring data availability for the analytical, monitoring and decision-making systems. At the present moment of time, this architecture is enabling scalable, interoperable and real-time data exchange, driving efficiency, predictive maintenance and smarter industrial operations in the era of Industry 4.0. This paper presents the design, development and integration of a sophisticated modern industrial automation system, which is based on MQTT and is representing the essence of the Industry 4.0 paradigm.

articleTitle: Xianhongshu’s Hashtag Utilization for Thai Fragrance Products on Cross-border E-commerce
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study analyzes user reviews and hashtag usage for Thai fragrance products on Xiaohongshu, a Chinese social electronic commerce platform. This study aims to explore how hashtags influence consumer engagement and sentiment toward Thai fragrances. By collecting and analyzing 60 Xiaohongshu posts related to Thai fragrances from January to November 2024 and performing sentiment analysis on the accompanying user reviews, this study identified key themes and consumer sentiment. The analysis showed that while high-frequency hashtags increase product awareness, low-frequency hashtags drive more meaningful engagement with niche audiences. Sentiment analysis revealed that most reviews were neutral, with positive reviews highlighting preferences for specific fragrances and negative reviews focusing on issues such as fragrance longevity and pricing. These findings provide valuable insights for Thai fragrance brands to optimize their marketing strategies on Xiaohongshu, focusing on improving product attributes and leveraging culturally relevant ingredients to better engage with consumers.

articleTitle: The GREENBEAT project: Optimizing Key Performance Indicators for Sustainable Excellence
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The greater mission of the project GREENBEAT is to raise awareness in the higher education sector of the importance of adopting and training skills for environmentally conscious and sustainable research and innovation approaches. The focus research area of GREENBEAT is Sustainable Future Communication Networks and Technologies, with an emphasis on networks and technologies for connecting intelligence and trustworthiness. One of the prerequisites to achieve this is to enlighten and engage the higher education sector on the paramount importance of integrating environmentally conscious and sustainable practices into research and innovation. With a strong emphasis on networks and technologies that bridge intelligence with trustworthiness, GREENBEAT aligns with the European Green Deal’s vision of a resource-efficient, competitive economy, aiming for zero net emissions by 2050. This paper illustrates the approach for the definition of a set of the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the impact towards the implementation of the project’s Research and Innovation (R&I) strategy. The selection of KPIs is done in such a way to allow an easy estimation of the progress and performance of the R&I for the achievement of its goals and objectives. In this context, the KPIs are related to the implementation of the major goals of the joint R&I strategy and reflect its outcomes.

articleTitle: OpenAI-Powered NLP for SQL Generation: Enhancing Database Access for Non-Technical Users
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Database accessibility can be challenging for users without technical expertise, particularly when generating SQL queries to retrieve information. This study addresses this gap by developing an OpenAI-powered system designed to automate SQL command generation, enabling non-expert users to interact with databases using natural language. Implemented as a web application, the system was evaluated by expert users, assessing both performance in query accuracy and user satisfaction. Results indicate high usability and satisfaction scores, with the system effectively enhancing accessibility to database functions, thus providing a user-friendly solution for database management.

articleTitle: An Application of SECI Model on Teaching Design and Practices in Chemistry Experiment Course
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study focuses on the application of the SECI model in chemistry experiment teaching to enhance students' ability to integrate chemistry knowledge and competitiveness. Current chemistry experiment teaching suffers from fragmented content and single teaching methods, leading to students' insufficient knowledge integration ability. This research adopts a mixed-methods approach, constructs a conceptual model based on the SECI model, encompassing four stages: socialization, externalization, combination, and internalization. Data is collected through observation, testing, and other methods, statistical analysis is used to evaluate teaching effectiveness. The study uses the salt hydrolysis experiment as the example. After practical application, an assessment is conducted. The expected outcomes of this research are to validate the effectiveness of the SECI model in chemistry experiment teaching, provide a practical teaching model, assist students in improving their chemical experiment capabilities, and contribute to the development of chemistry education.

articleTitle: Automating Persona Generation: Leveraging ChatGPT-4 in Educational Digital Services
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research provides a preliminary study on automating user persona generation via ChatGPT-4 with a case study on educational digital services. Data were collected from 40 undergraduate students at one of Thailand’s science and technology higher education institutes through questionnaires and semi-structured interviews, with participants grouped via K-means clustering based on similar responses. The study relied on ChatGPT-4 to generate personas based on empathy maps, jobs-to-be-done analysis, and Hofstede’s cultural dimensions. The validity of the generated personas was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations to identify key influencing features, revealing that integrating cultural contexts enhances persona specificity and relevance. The findings demonstrate that personas generated through this approach accurately reflect unique traits of target clusters, while significantly reducing the time and resources required. This study highlights a practical method for using ChatGPT-4 to generate personas, focusing on Thai science and tech undergraduates. It shows how tailored data collection improves ChatGPT’s understanding of specific user groups. Future research could expand sample sizes and explore broader contexts to enable generalization of the approach to become a framework that works across multiple target users and application contexts. Additionally, exploring methods like hierarchical K-means may improve clustering accuracy. Incorporating expert evaluations using the Persona Perception Scale could further ensure the real-world applicability.

articleTitle: Integrating Marker-based Augmented Reality into Serious Games for Disaster Risk Management Training: Preliminary Technical Insights from the Philippines
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Serious games are emerging as promising training tools for disaster risk management as they provide experiential learning in a safe simulated environment. Given limited attention of learners, this study explores the integration of marker-based Augmented Reality (AR) into three serious games developed by researchers from the University of the Philippines. It discusses the development, implementation and deployment of a web-based AR application and examines its effects on perception and propensity towards serious games. Technical details such as development frameworks, software libraries, and deployment methods are also discussed. Beyond the potential of augmented learning, this study establishes a foundation for future AR-based development for DRM capacity building.

articleTitle: Developing a RAG Agent for Personalized Fitness and Dietary Guidance
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper focuses on implementing and evaluating a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that provides personalized fitness and dietary guidance by combining real-time data from wearable devices with curated knowledge sources. While the current implementation depends on a carefully selected set of PDF files as a source of knowledge base, extracting relevant information in order to frame the answer to a question by the user, the planned integration of a curated, well-structured database aims to enhance the system’s reliability and scope. The paper presents an overview of RAG-based system-related literature, describes the process of implementing the RAG component, and discusses the effectiveness in generating relevant and accurate answers. This implementation demonstrates the capability of RAG technology to develop interactive and effective solutions for dietary and fitness applications and sets a foundation for further system improvements.

articleTitle: Exploring Young Students’ Experiences in IoT Skill Development Through Peer-Assisted Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: While existing literature provides insights into the benefits of IoT and Peer-Assisted Learning (PAL) individually, a gap remains in understanding how secondary school students perceive and experience IoT skill development through PAL. Using qualitative methods, this study aims to explore the experiences of secondary school students participating in a PAL program focused on IoT skill development. Five students from Mechai Bamboo School participated in the research: three from grade 11, one from grade 9, and one from grade 7, selected randomly. Thematic analysis of the data revealed that students perceived PAL as offering peer-led learning comfort, practical application confidence, collaborative problem-solving, mentor communication support, and enhanced learning retention. Understanding students’ perspectives on PAL in relation to IoT education could improve the design and implementation of similar programs in secondary schools.

articleTitle: Development of a Closed Chamber System for Cultivating Lion's Mane Mushrooms using an Internet of Things System to Increase Yield and Economic Value
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research investigates the development and implementation of an Internet of Things (IoT)-based closedsystem prototype for cultivating Yamabushitake (Lion's Mane) mushrooms, addressing the challenges of achieving optimal yields in Thailand's climate. Conducted at Saengkaew Mushroom Farm located in Nan Province, the study focuses on precise environmental control within the prototype chamber. The system employs an ESP32-IOXESP32U microcontroller and an AM2315 sensor to monitor and manage temperature, humidity, and airflow. A comparative analysis with a traditional evaporative cooling system reveals the closed system's superior performance in achieving higher yields and improved energy efficiency. The assessment of economic feasibility is conducted via a Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA), demonstrating the potential for increased profitability and sustainable mushroom cultivation. This research offers significant findings regarding the utilization of IoT technology to enhance mushroom production and advance sustainable agricultural practices in Thailand.

articleTitle: Enhancing LMS Design through SUS Analysis and Biometric Usability Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of e-learning platforms, especially Learning Management Systems (LMS), there have been increasing issues in achieving a seamless user experience. Although LMS are becoming integrated into the traditional education system, they often fail to meet the expectations of students and lecturers, which causes the dissatisfaction and frustration. This study examines the usability of the LMS at Mae Fah Luang University by applying both traditional System Usability Scale (SUS) surveys and refined biometric usability testing, using facial expression analysis and respiratory data collection. These dual techniques ensure to uncover the deeper knowledge into the emotion and cognitive states of the users while they are interacting with the LMS. The SUS survey showed the navigation issues and user interface (UI) complexity, with the poor usability score of 55. Biometric data analysis then emphasized and validated these findings, by revealing the negative emotions together with fluctuated respiratory patterns. SUS and biometric approach to usability testing focus on requirements of implementing an intuitive and user-friendly LMS design to improve the learning experience of the students. Recommendations encompass the information visibility, clear navigation paths and timely notification to improve overall usability of LMS.

articleTitle: Evaluating Large Language Models: Challenges, Limitations, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed Natural Language Processing (NLP) by providing previously unheard-of capabilities in text production, translation, and comprehension. Large Language Models have advanced rapidly. Nevertheless, there are several obstacles and restrictions associated with the implementation and assessment of these models. This study offers a thorough analysis of the situation of LLMs today, with an emphasis on the methods for assessing their effectiveness and significance. Key issues like prejudice, moral dilemmas, scalability, and transparency are noted, and the shortcomings of the current frameworks for evaluation are also covered. Our goal in examining these problems is to identify the areas that require improvement. In addition, we suggest possible direction for future investigation, stressing the importance of inclusive datasets, improved interpretability, and stronger assessment criteria. In addition to guiding the creation of more morally and effectively constructed AI systems, our mission is to promote a greater understanding of LLMs.

articleTitle: Classification Model of Dementia and Heart Failure in Older Adults Using Extra Trees and Oversampling-Based Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Dementia (DM) and heart failure (HF) are prevalent and concerning medical conditions among older adults. Several studies indicate that individuals with HF have more risk of developing DM, underscoring the significant correlation between these two conditions. This proposed classification model employed Extra Trees (ETs) to develop a classification model for dementia and heart failure from electronic health records from Chiangrai Prachanukroh Hospital in Chiang Rai Province, Thailand, totally 4,297 records. The imbalanced data was addressed by using Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique for Nominal and Continuous (SMOTENC). Its performance was evaluated against other methods, including Decision Trees (DT), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), and Adaptive Boosting (AB). The findings indicated that the proposed ET model surpasses alternative methods in accuracy (89.11%), precision (94.92%), recall (92.50%), F-measure (93.70%), and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC) score (78.88%).

articleTitle: Development of a Virtual Reality World for Avatar Thai Costume Dressing with Integrated e-Commerce System
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study presents the development and evaluation of a Virtual Reality (VR) system designed to revolutionize the shopping experience for traditional Thai textiles. The system integrates customizable avatars and e-commerce functionalities, enabling users to explore, personalize, and purchase traditional Thai attire in an immersive virtual environment. High-quality 3D models and intricate textile designs emphasize the cultural heritage and craftsmanship of Thai textiles, particularly from the Roi-Kaen-Sarn-Sin cluster, which comprises four provinces: Roi Et, Khon Kaen, Maha Sarakham, and Kalasin. Expert assessments rated the performance efficiency with an average score of 4.52, while user evaluations provided an average satisfaction score of 4.14. Although the system demonstrates significant potential, opportunities remain for optimizing scalability and user accessibility. This research underscores the transformative potential of VR technology in creating immersive shopping experiences, fostering cultural appreciation, and driving innovation in global e-commerce markets.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Consumer Preferences and Purchasing Behavior of Thai Herbal Products in the Chinese Market of Gold Mint Products Co., Ltd
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study investigates Chinese consumers' behavior and preferences in purchasing Thai herbal products, focusing on Gold Mint Products Co., Ltd, a prominent Thai inhaler company, as a case study. The research background section outlines the growing market potential for Thai herbal products and the increasing interest among Chinese consumers. The literature review provides an in-depth analysis of the global herbal market and discusses the current status of Thai herbs in the international market. It also explores the key factors that influence consumer purchasing decisions. Using 4P marketing as a theoretical framework, the application of the 4P marketing strategy to Thai herbal companies in four aspects—product, price, place, and promotion, is analyzed. The methodology section describes the questionnaire design, sample size, data collection and data analysis methods in detail. The results reveal the key factors that influence Chinese consumers' purchasing preferences. This study provides valuable insights for Thai herbal product exporters, helping them to better understand the needs and expectations of Chinese consumers, and provides practical suggestions for optimizing marketing strategies and improving market competitiveness. In addition, these suggestions also provide feasible directions and opportunities for Thai exporters to expand into other international markets.

articleTitle: Exploration and Exploitation of Consumers' Purchasing Factors based on Fan Economy for Thai Products
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous development of e-commerce, fan economy has attracted more and more attention from everyone, and it is emerging as a new consumption model, which has an impact on consumers' purchase decisions. In this case, social media is playing an increasingly critical role, not only to facilitate fan interaction, but also to influence consumer spending patterns. The purpose of this study is to identify the key influencing factors of the fan economy in purchasing decisions. The findings will inform the development of practical marketing strategies for Thai brands entering the Chinese market, with a particular focus on leveraging social media to enhance interactions between fans and brands.

articleTitle: A Study of Factors Affecting the Students' Computer Programming Achievement Using Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Acquiring computer programming skills frequently poses difficulties for students because it necessitates analytical reasoning, logical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. The challenges of mastering programming syntax and debugging errors contribute to elevated dropout rates and diminished engagement. This research utilizes machine learning methodologies to forecast students' academic performance in computer programming and discern critical factors influencing their success. A Support Vector Machine (SVM) model was employed in two iterations of analysis involving 750 records. The initial round encompassed all 29 attributes, whereas the subsequent round concentrated on five principal attributes determined via multiple regression analysis. The research identified five principal attributes—high school GPA, self-directed learning attitude, experience with programming flowcharts, learning style preference, and career motivation—as significant predictors of learning outcomes in computer programming, attaining an accuracy of 72.40%. This allows educators to customize approaches, including the simplification of intricate subjects, the integration of experiential activities, and the provision of additional resources such as exercises and tutorials, to enhance student.

articleTitle: Ensemble Approaches for Quartz and Silica Gel Identification using EDX spectra
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: During a manufacturing process, hard disk drive (HDD) might be contaminated by some materials such as Quartz and Silica Gel. These contaminations induce a major failure in the HDD. Identifying them is a necessary approach to track back to the sources and prevent this issue to happen again in the future. In this work, we are interested in identifying Quartz and Silica Gel by analyzing their spectra obtained from using an Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX) instrument. A challenge is that these two materials are from the same functional group (Silicon Dioxide) and have quite similar EDX spectra which cause a classifying problem to experts. In this work, we proposed a parallel ensemble learning approach based on EDX spectra to improve the classification between Quartz and Silica Gel. Four ensemble methods were studied and compared: Hard Voting, Soft Voting, Weighted Hard Voting, and Weighted Soft Voting. We applied and chose the base models of the ensemble methods from 12 well-known machine learning (ML) models. Experimental results show that the Soft Voting and Weighted Soft Voting techniques achieved a maximum accuracy of 82.5% and significantly outperformed individual ML models in classifying Quartz and Silica Gel.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Semi Management and Full Management Models on Cross-Border E-Commerce Platforms
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Cross-border e-commerce is developing rapidly. The full management model lowers the threshold but has high costs and strong platform dependence; the semi management model is flexible and efficient, attracting more sellers. This study compares and analyzes the two models, explores their strengths, weaknesses and trends, and provides a reference for sellers to choose a platform.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Pose Identification System with Force-Sensitive Resistors for Four-Step Balance Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study proposes a system to identify poses based on the 4-stage balance test for fall risk assessment using custom-developed, pressure-sensitive footwear equipped with force-sensitive resistors (FSRs) and machine learning (ML) models. The system captures and analyzes pressure distribution data during balance tests to predict types of poses. Data was collected from 30 healthy participants aged 18-25 years performing standard balance tests. Preprocessing steps included data cleaning, normalization, and feature extraction. Three ML models—Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Random Forest (RF), and Gradient Boosting (GB)—were evaluated. The LSTM model achieved the highest performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores, demonstrating its capability in handling sequential data. The system shows promise as a cost-effective tool for pose identification to aid fall risk assessment, though further research is needed to expand the dataset diversity and refine the algorithms. This study provides a foundation for developing scalable tools to assess and mitigate fall risks, particularly among vulnerable populations.

articleTitle: Emotion Classification Using Transformer-Based Language Model
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper presents Emotion Classification Using Transformer-Based Language Models, highlighting the growing interest in emotion-related studies, particularly in the Thai language. Emotions play a crucial role in perception, influencing text input on various platforms or responses in chatbot interactions. Text messages, when combined into sentences, may convey diverse emotions, leading to misunderstandings and potentially inappropriate behavior. To classify emotions in text, experiments were conducted using a dataset from the Jubjai chatbot. The study aimed to identify the most effective pre-trained model and compare the results of data cleansing between fine-tuned and non-fine-tuned models to evaluate the accuracy in analyzing 7, 5, and 3 emotions. The experimental results demonstrated that the fine-tuned Wangchangberta model outperformed XLM-RoBERTa, achieving accuracy rates of 73% for 7 emotions, 76% for 5 emotions, and 82% for 3 emotions.

articleTitle: A Kano Model Approach to Design Northern Thai Local Experiences Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study finds that tourists are interested in local experiences. With the Internet, travel platforms are a necessity for tourists., and Northern Thailand is one of the most attractive regions for Chinese tourists. This paper analyses the features and functionality of a tourism platform designed to provide Chinese tourists with a local experience of Northern Thailand. This study aims to: (1) develop standards for features and content that enhance the local experience on travel platforms (based on expert interviews), (2) classify platform features according to Chinese tourists' preferences (using the Kano model). Data was collected through questionnaires distributed on Chinese social media and targeted platforms. The sample included four tourism industry experts for interview and 190 responses form questionnaire, of which 147 were valid, And this study identifies key features of travel platforms that appeal to Chinese tourists. The findings provide new insights for the development of tourism platforms or online marketing strategies targeting Chinese tourists, particularly for Northern Thailand, to enhance tourism development in the region.

articleTitle: Thai Beef Cattle Recognition for Fattening Farms: An Empirical Study of Cattle Cooperative Practices in Chiang Rai
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research focuses on developing an automated system to identify the breed and sex of Thai beef cattle using advanced computer vision technology. By using the YOLOv11 (You Only Look Once) model, a state-of-the-art object detection tool, this system can quickly and accurately identify cattle breeds and determine their sex. High-resolution image datasets were collected and augmented, yielding 81.2% accuracy for breed detection and 95.0% for sex classification, with mAP@50 scores of 85.1% and 99.3%, respectively. However, limited data for certain breeds, like Thai Native and Japanese cattle, reduced the model’s performance for those categories. To overcome this, we aim to expand the dataset from CCTV footage in future studies. The system will include user-friendly features, such as real-time alerts and dashboards, making it practical for farmers to use. This project demonstrates how AI can improve cattle farming by saving time, reducing errors, and supporting better decisions. Future improvements will explore applications in disease detection and behavior monitoring.

articleTitle: Growing Beautifully at Regina Coeli: Award-Winning LINE Stickers Reflecting School Values and Identity
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Regina Coeli College, founded in 1932 as the only Catholic all-girls school in Chiang Mai, Thailand, is committed to nurturing knowledgeable, confident, and virtuous young women while honoring its rich cultural and historical heritage. Rooted in the spirit of Serviam ("I will serve"), the school emphasizes love, compassion, and community service as core values. To celebrate and communicate this identity, the LINE sticker set "Growing Beautifully at Regina Coeli" was developed, featuring 16 intricately designed illustrations that encapsulate the school’s values of love, happiness, friendship, and growth. Created using Adobe Illustrator and meeting LINE’s technical standards, the stickers seamlessly bridge generations, blending tradition with modern digital expression to foster connections among students, alumni, parents, and faculty. Awarded first prize in the WE ARE SERVIAM LINE Sticker Contest and released in September 2024, the stickers have gained widespread popularity, with sales proceeds supporting school activities and reinforcing its mission. This initiative demonstrates the transformative potential of digital media in preserving cultural heritage, enhancing engagement, and showcasing a model for educational branding that unites tradition with innovation, ensuring Regina Coeli’s identity remains impactful and relevant in the rapidly evolving digital landscape.

articleTitle: Leveraging Historical Artwork as Digital Arts Inspiration with The See -Think -Wonder -Investigate Imagine (STWII) Thinking Routine
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper investigates how historical painting like the persistence of memory by Salvador Dali can become inspiration in creating new digital artworks through the See-Think-Wonder-Investigate-Imagine (STWI-I) thinking routine. STWI-I is a thinking routine that is developed from artful thinking, a pedagocial approach to enhance cognitive skills through art. The STWI-I routine guided students in the whole learning experience starting from observing historical artworks, analyzing their significance, asking critical questions, investigating further by conducting research, and creating new digital artworks inspired by historical movements. The study found that the application of the STWI-I routine significantly improved students' ability to analyze and synthesize important information about the artwork, using it as inspiration to create new pieces. This approach not only fostered creativity and cognitive skills by incorporating the artists' methods into their projects but also led to a deeper understanding of both the historical context and their own creative processes. The findings demonstrate that taking historical artworks as inspiration in art education enriches the creative process and broadens students' artistic capabilities. Future research could further explore the STWI-I approach's applications in various artistic disciplines beyond painting and educational contexts.

articleTitle: Improving Robotics and IoT Learning Achievement in Junior High School Students through a Constructionist Project-Based Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: While many studies have explored the impact of project-based learning (PBL) on robotics education, none have done so within a constructionist academic framework. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the constructionist PBL approach in enhancing the robotics and IoT learning achievements of junior high school students. The participants included 18 eighth-grade Darunsikkhalai School for Innovative Learning students, selected through purposeful sampling techniques. The experiment spanned 10 weeks, with data collected before and after the intervention using a test to assess learning achievements in Robotics and IoT. The paired-sample t-test results indicated a significant improvement in the students’ learning achievements in these areas. This study provides valuable insights into the potential benefits of integrating constructionist principles with PBL in modern educational settings, ultimately fostering a deeper understanding and proficiency in robotics and IoT among young learners.

articleTitle: AI for Healthcare: A Classification Model for Personalized Premenstrual Symptoms and Depressive Crisis Risk Tracking Using Data Analytics and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: A significant obstacle to women's lives is menstruation, which, in some cases, leads to depression, anxiety, and stress. This research, therefore, aims to solve this problem with three objectives: to study the context of female adolescents who experience premenstrual syndrome (PMS) problems and depression crises, to develop a classification model for personalized premenstrual symptoms and depressive crisis risk tracking using data analytics and machine learning techniques, and to evaluate the performance of all developed models to select suitable models for future application. The research data included 282 volunteers who gave consent from the University of Phayao, with random sampling. The machine learning used in this research consists of six techniques: decision trees, k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, naïve bayes, random forests, and support vector machines. The model performance is tested using 10-fold cross-validation and evaluated using five metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score, and time. The results of the construction and evaluation of all models are at a high level, which is encouraging. The researchers expect that this research can be further developed for future mobile applications.

articleTitle: Orthopedic Walker Fall Detection and Motion Classification Using Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Accurate fall detection for orthopedic walker users is essential for timely medical intervention and enhancing safety for elderly and mobility-impaired individuals. This paper introduces a new method using a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) neural network to detect falls and classify motion patterns in walker usage. We use the Walker dataset, which includes inertial measurement unit sensor data for four motion classes: idle, motion, step, and fall. The dataset consists of 6-axis IMU readings (3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyroscope) from sensors mounted on orthopedic walkers, with around 620 samples per class. Our BiGRU model leverages temporal dependencies in both forward and backward directions to improve classification accuracy. We assess the model’s performance in two scenarios: binary classification (fall vs. non-fall) and multi-class classification of all four motion types. The proposed architecture shows strong performance, achieving 99.79% accuracy and a 99.73% F1-score in binary classification, and 98.51% accuracy and a 98.50% F1-score in multi-class classification. It outperforms traditional deep learning models like CNN, LSTM, and GRU. The experimental results confirm the effectiveness of bidirectional processing in capturing temporal motion patterns, indicating significant potential for realtime fall detection in walker-assisted mobility. The high precision and recall values in both scenarios demonstrate the model’s reliability for practical healthcare monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cultural Tourism with VR: A Virtual Tour of Wat Pho
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an interactive virtual reality (VR) web application for exploring Wat Pho, a UNESCO Memory of the World heritage site in Bangkok, Thailand. Aimed at enhancing cultural tourism and accessibility, the application provides a 360° virtual tour of key locations within the temple grounds. Developed using Unity and Firebase, the application integrates interactive elements such as navigational arrows, Thai audio narration, textual information, and a chatbot for user queries. This immersive VR experience offers a novel way to engage with Wat Pho’s rich history and cultural significance for both local and remote audiences, overcoming barriers of physical access.

articleTitle: Mitigating Data Sparsity in Point-of-Interest Recommendation Systems Using Multi-Modal User Profiles
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This study presents a solution to the data sparsity issue in POI recommendation systems by introducing a multi-modal user profile approach called Visual-Textual Collaborative Filtering (VTCF). VTCF integrates textual POI descriptions from Wikipedia with user-generated photos to improve the representation of user preferences. Using publicly available geo-tagged photo datasets, we compared VTCF with various baseline methods, including traditional user-based collaborative filtering and approaches based on visual and contextual preferences. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach successfully addresses the challenges of sparse check-in data, resulting in more accurate and relevant recommendations. The findings suggest that VTCF is a promising method for improving recommendation accuracy. Future work could explore additional data sources and techniques to further enhance POI recommendation systems. Moreover, computational trade-offs and scalability should be considered, as integrating textual and visual data adds system complexity. Strategies such as batch processing and parallel computation could help mitigate these issues for large-scale applications.

articleTitle: Main Difficulties in Mental Counselling among Counsellors in Higher Vocational Colleges
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: As society has developed, a range of social contradictions have emerged, highlighting the complex nature of mental health issues. In particular, a number of college students are suffering from mental health problems to some degree. Meanwhile, school counsellors play an essential role in solving students' mental problems. Therefore, this study is to explore the challenges of mental health counselling for counsellors in higher vocational colleges. The research collected factors through semi-structured interviews based on the four aspects of the ecological model of mental health theory-the individual level, the interpersonal level, the community level, and the social level. The results identified practical bottlenecks for counsellors in dealing with students' mental problems in higher vocational colleges and revealed the limitations of the existing mental support system in terms of professionalism, resource allocation, and collaborative mechanisms. This paper will help improve theoretical understanding of the difficulties faced by counsellors in mental counselling and optimize counselling practice.

articleTitle: Enhancing Social and Economic Well-being through Smart Farming: A Case Study in Pa-Laew Pak Dee Dee, Nan, Thailand
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research examines the challenges and opportunities facing elderly farmers in rural Nan Province. Using a qualitative approach, the study explores retirement plans, the state of the agricultural sector, and the potential of smart agriculture. Findings highlight the need for policies supporting both elderly farmers while attracting younger generations to agriculture. The study recommends strategies to promote wider adoption of smart agriculture in remote areas, addressing challenges in the domain of irrigation, declining farming capabilities, and cost.

articleTitle: BPMN Implementation Challenges When Used for Service Orchestration
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: The adoption of BPMN-based process orchestration has increased more recently. With this adoption, we have witnessed growing challenges while implementing BPMN-based software architectures. This paper aims to study the challenges faced during the implementation of BPMN 2.0 used to orchestrate REST, SOAP, or other web services and to create a higher level of capability service to provide an orchestrated backend to the UI application. The paper goes through the existing literature and then delves into the challenges of considering the real-world use case to discuss the pros and cons. It also provides a prescriptive architecture to set the guidelines for BPMN 2.0 usage in service orchestration.

articleTitle: A Case Study on Digital Marketing and Consumer Behavior for Cheongsam Sales Targeting Chinese Female Customers in Chiang Mai
publicationTitle: 2025 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: As a symbol of traditional Chinese culture, the cheongsam has regained global attention in modern design. This research focuses on the Chinese female community in Chiang Mai, Thailand, to explore the sales potential of cheongsams in this market.
